variants.title: Clinical thermometer: a normal body temperature
variants.unknown: the body temperature in degrees Celsius
variants.note: The normal temperature of the human body is about 37 °C; it varies a little from person to person and through the day.

source.title: Science, Textbook for Class VII, NCERT - Heat (normal human body temperature about 37 °C)

variants.title: Clinical thermometer: a patient with fever
variants.sample: A patient running a fever (temperature unknown)
variants.note: The kink in the tube holds the thread, so the reading can be taken after the thermometer is out of the mouth.

source.title: Curiosity, Science Textbook for Class VI, NCERT - Temperature and its Measurement (clinical thermometer 35 to 42 °C)

variants.title: Laboratory thermometer: warm water in a beaker
variants.sample: Warm water in the beaker (temperature unknown)
variants.note: This is well outside 35 to 42 °C, so the clinical thermometer cannot be used at all: it would burst.

source.title: Curiosity, Science Textbook for Class VI, NCERT - Temperature and its Measurement (laboratory thermometer -10 to 110 °C)

variants.title: Laboratory thermometer: ice-cold water
variants.sample: Water with melting ice in it (temperature unknown)
variants.unknown: the temperature of the cold water
variants.note: Below the clinical thermometer's range: again, only the laboratory thermometer will do.

source.title: Curiosity, Science Textbook for Class VI, NCERT - Temperature and its Measurement
